subject: POC Trial: Workload Intake & Success Criteria
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: POC Trial: Workload Intake & Success Criteria

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great discussion. Per our agreement, I wanted to capture the post-call recap and next steps for the POC/trial so we can align on success criteria, evaluation plan, and the workload profile we'll load against Redwood.

Summary / Success criteria (proposal):
- Latency: 95th percentile latency for 1k-token prompts should be <= 500ms per request under target concurrency (see below).
- Throughput & Stability: system sustained at 30 RPS with spikes to 75 RPS for short bursts without error-rate > 1%.
- Cost baseline: token costs and compute footprint agree within +/- 15% of Redwood's estimation after 72 hours of representative traffic.
- Quality: model outputs meet your internal QA for the scoring rubric we discussed (intent match, hallucination rate, token budget).

Workload / traffic intake (what we need from you):
- Typical RPS: 20-30 RPS sustained (confirm average).
- Peak bursts: up to ~75 RPS for 60-120s, mostly during shift changes.
- Concurrency: 40-50 concurrent requests typical during peak windows.
- Prompt lengths: median prompt ~300 tokens, 95th percentile ~1,200 tokens; expected response length median 120 tokens.
- Session behavior / KV cache usage: many repeated prefixes for patient-summary retrieval — expect high cache hit rate if supported.

Attachments: I attached the workload intake template (acmehealth-workload-template.xlsx) and our POC checklist (redwood-poc-checklist.pdf). Please populate the intake tab with real numbers where possible.

Proposed timeline / owners:
- This week (by Fri 7/17): AcmeHealth to fill workload intake + share any sample logs / example prompts (owner: Priya).
- Week of 7/20: Redwood to provision trial environment and run initial soak tests (owner: Marissa).
- Week of 7/27: Joint evaluation week, run quality checks + cost reconciliation (owners: Ben / Alex / Marissa).

Next steps (short list):
1) Priya: send completed workload template + sample prompts/logs.
2) Marissa: confirm GPU profile and estimated capacity for the trial (I'll defer to you for the exact instance sizes).
3) Ben: schedule a 30-min sync for 7/21 to review test plan and monitoring dashboards.

Thanks — happy to adjust any of the success criteria if you have internal constraints or different SLAs.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Executive
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: acmehealth-workload-template.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-poc-checklist.pdf (pdf)

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-15T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC Trial: Workload Intake & Success Criteria

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. We're aligned on most of this. A few clarifications and notes from our infra/ops team: 

- Sustained RPS: Our current prod-ish traffic for the pilot scope averages about 25 RPS during business hours; night windows drop to ~3-4 RPS.
- Bursts: The 75 RPS figure is accurate for the regional hubs during handoffs; sometimes we see brief spikes to ~100 RPS for 30-45s when multiple clinics close simultaneously.
- Token distributions: I'll attach a redacted sample of recent prompts (sensitive data removed) — see attached sample_prompts_redacted.txt. Median prompt closer to 280 tokens; 95th at ~1,100.
- Authentication: We will use our existing SSO and will share service account creds for the trial; need to confirm the secret rotation cadence.

I've attached the filled intake tab (acmehealth-workload-template.xlsx) — it's preliminary but should give you what you need to size the initial capacity. We'll clean up the remaining rows by EOD Thursday.

One ask: can Redwood include KV cache behavior in the trial perf tests? Our access patterns should benefit a prefix cache. If yes, Marissa, can you confirm how you'll simulate repeated prefixes?

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Director, Clinical Engineering
AcmeHealth

---
Attachments: acmehealth-workload-template.xlsx (updated), sample_prompts_redacted.txt (txt)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-16T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC Trial: Workload Intake & Success Criteria

Thanks Priya — got the intake sheet and the sample prompts. High level on Redwood side:

- Provisioning: I'll stand up a Dedicated trial cluster with the GPU profile we discussed (A6000-equivalent nodes, auto-scaling to handle bursts).
- KV cache: we can simulate prefix-heavy traffic by replaying your sample prompts with controlled prefix repeats; Dylan will own the test harness scripting.
- Monitoring: we'll provide dashboards with per-route latency, token consumption, and error breakdowns; we can also surface 95/99p and backend GPU utilization.
- Cost estimate: preliminary estimate attached in the POC checklist doc; final numbers after 72-hr soak test.

Dylan — can you take the sample_prompts_redacted.txt and produce a replay plan? Goal is to run:
- Soak: 72 hours at 30 RPS steady state.
- Burst tests: 3 runs of 90-120s at 100 RPS.
- Concurrency profile: ramp to 50 concurrent requests and hold for 10 minutes in the middle of each soak.

Priya — two quick questions for your team:
1) Are there hard rate limits or throttles on your side we should be aware of when we drive spikes?
2) Do you have a preferred window for the 72-hr soak (we were thinking starting 7/21 08:00 PT)?

I'll own infra provisioning and baseline metrics; Ben, I'll sync with you on the stakeholder update once we have soak results.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference

Perfect — thanks everyone for the quick turn. Quick confirmation of next steps and owners: 

- Priya (AcmeHealth): finalize and re-send the workload intake with any additional throttling notes by EOD 7/17.
- Marissa (Redwood): provision the trial cluster and share monitoring links by 7/20.
- Dylan (Redwood): deliver replay harness and test schedule; begin soak on 7/21 08:00 PT if no objections.
- Ben (Redwood): schedule 30-min sync on 7/21 11:00 PT (invitation to follow).

If anyone needs to shift the start window for the soak, please flag before EOD Monday 7/20. Looking forward to the trial — we should be able to get actionable perf and cost data quickly.

Best,
Ben Carter
